newsitem.title: UK: British budget to keep mortgage relief - report.
newsitem.headline: British budget to keep mortgage relief - report.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown has rejected proposals by Treasury officials to abolish mortgage tax relief in his first budget, the Sunday Times newspaper said.
A Treasury official said the report was "speculation" ahead of the new Labour government's first budget on July 2.
Labour refused to commit itself to maintaining relief on homeowners' loans in its election manifesto, the newspaper said, raising fears of its imminent abolition.
But Labour promised not to increase the standard or top rates of income tax and to live within tight spending limits set by its Conservative predecessors.
The centrepiece of the budget will be a one-off "windfall tax" on the profits of privatised utility companies.
But economists expect a cut in advance corporation tax (ACT), which, conversely, raises revenue by reducing the tax credits companies receive on dividend payments.
They also expect a limit to tax relief on allowances, to the basic rate.
